research.facts:
HARPPA Nordi Toddler Tower Stool Recall
**Source 1:** cpsc.gov/Recalls/2026/HARPPA-Recalls-Nordi-Toddler-Tower-Stools-Due-to-Risk-of-Serious-Injury-and-Death-from-Entrapment-and-Fall-Hazards
- Official CPSC recall page
- Model: HANS0002 (label on underside of stool platform)
- Units: ~47,166
- Hazards: collapse/tip-over; child's torso can fit through front/back openings (entrapment)
- Incidents: 3 reports of collapsing/tipping; 2 injuries (scrapes, cuts, bruises)
- Description: white, black and blue stool with natural wood color on step/platform/safety bars; ~18in deep, 18in wide, 38.6in tall
- Price: ~$130
- Sold: harppababy.com and Amazon.com; September 2023 – June 2026
- Remedy: FREE repair kit from HARPPA (protective nets, stabilizing feet, installation instructions); includes shipping
- Contact: harppababy.com for repair kit
- Confidence: HIGH (primary source: CPSC.gov official recall)
**Source 2:** medicaldaily.com/toddler-kitchen-tower-stool-recall-cpsc-entrapment-2026-476739
- Headline: "Federal Regulators Recall 138,000 Toddler Kitchen Towers Because a Child's Torso Can Fit Through the Side Openings" — NOTE: This article appears to aggregate multiple recalls. The HARPPA recall alone is ~47,166 units. The 138,000 figure likely includes other brands.
- Do NOT use 138,000 figure for HARPPA — use 47,166 from CPSC.gov
- Confidence: MEDIUM (aggregation article; primary facts from CPSC)
**Source 3:** karmactive.com/harppa-nordi-toddler-tower-recall-entrapment-fall/
- Additional coverage confirming CPSC recall details
- Confidence: HIGH (consistent with CPSC.gov)
**Source 4:** x.com/USCPSC/status/2082905780529910250
- CPSC official X post: "HARPPA Recalls Nordi Toddler Tower Stools; The recalled tower stools can collapse or tip over while in use. Get Repair."
- Confidence: HIGH (official CPSC account)
**KEY FACTS (HIGH confidence):**
- Unit count: ~47,166
- Model: HANS0002
- Recall hazard: collapse/tip-over + entrapment (torso fits through openings)
- Injuries: 3 incidents, 2 injuries (scrapes/cuts/bruises)
- Price when sold: ~$130
- Where sold: Amazon.com, harppababy.com
- Sale dates: Sep 2023 – Jun 2026
- Remedy: Free repair kit (contact HARPPA at harppababy.com)
- Stop use immediately

research.facts:
AAP Screen Time Guidelines
**Source 1:** health.choc.org/updated-aap-recommendations-for-screen-time
- CHOC (Children's Health) article on AAP updated screen time recommendations
- AAP 2026 update: prioritizes quality, context and conversation over strict time limits
- Key recommendations:
- Under 18 months: no screens except video calls (FaceTime, etc.)
- Ages 2-5: limit to 1 hour/day of high-quality programming
- Ages 6+: consistent limits protecting sleep, physical activity, family time
- Confidence: HIGH (CHOC is official children's hospital citing AAP guidelines)
**Source 2:** aap.org/en/news-room/news-releases-from-pediatrics/
- AAP official news releases
- Pediatrics journal Volume 158, Issue 3 (September 2026)
- Confidence: HIGH (official AAP source)
**KEY FACTS (HIGH confidence):**
- Organization: American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP)
- Update year: 2026
- Key shift: from strict time limits to quality + context + conversation focus
- Under 18 months: no screens (except video calls)
- Ages 2-5: max 1 hour/day of high-quality content
- Ages 6+: consistent limits; screens should not displace sleep, physical activity, homework
- Co-viewing encouraged: watch with children, discuss what you're watching
- Confidence: HIGH
